A known-bad control got waved through as harmless connective prose. That's a real gap in the instrument, not a clean sweep — 3 of 4, not 4 of 4.

**1. Defective entries (absent/spliced), 23 flagged by the sweep:**
44, 66, 77, 99, 34, 155, 7, 60, 126, 50, 61, 74, 120, 164, 102, 182, 199, 214, 218, 220, 221, 224, 225.
True count is at least 24 once you add the missed control (166), and the real number is probably higher — see point 4.

**2. Defect rate.** 106 entries total. One source (id 208, Sber/GigaChat docs) was never reachable — a JS-rendered SPA curl can't see through — so it's neither a pass nor a fail; exclude it. Denominator = 105 checkable entries. 23/105 ≈ **22%**. With the missed control folded in, ≈23%.

**3. Pattern.** Two distinct failure modes, and they don't overlap much:
- The bulk of "quotes" in this register (roughly two-thirds of all 106 entries) are apostrophe-boundary artifacts — the register's own analytical prose ("Anthropic's...", "it's...", "the candidate's...") accidentally captured as if it were a quotation, because whatever built this file split on apostrophes rather than real quote marks. That's a pipeline bug, not a sourcing bug, and it's the majority of what `not-a-source-quote` means here.
- The genuine defects cluster in two shapes: (a) ellipsis-spliced quotations that weld two real, non-adjacent sentences/sections into a claim the source never made as a unit (77, 99, 34, 182, 218, 220, 224, 225, 66) — hits every major vendor, not one; (b) invented numbers presented as fact (44: 75% vs. actual 90%; 50: fabricated 59–498% vs. actual 525%/50–525%/75%; 185: DeepSeek cache prices that match no column on the live page). No vintage trend by id number, but 5 of the last 8 entries checked (218, 220, 221, 224, 225) are defective — quality did not improve toward the end of the run.

**4. What this sweep didn't cover.** It only checked whether a bracketed fragment is a literal substring of the source. Once something got bucketed `not-a-source-quote`, the underlying factual claim mostly went unchecked — id 185's fabricated DeepSeek prices only got caught because that particular agent happened to fact-check further; dozens of other `not-a-source-quote` entries got no such follow-through. Id 208 remains genuinely unresolved (SPA, unreachable), so its quoted claim is unverified, not confirmed either way — don't read its absence of a "hits: 0" as a clean result. Paywalled/secondary sources (id 66's underlying "The Information" piece) were explicitly left unchecked. And several "verbatim" hits are only confirmed against duplicated hydration-JSON copies embedded in the fetched HTML, not cross-checked against whether that content is stale relative to the live rendered page.
